extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, professional representatives, and EPO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Official EPO Guidelines setting out practice and procedure for examination, search, opposition and related proceedings under the European Patent Convention, covering formalities, substantive requirements (patentability, unity, sufficiency, clarity, priority) and rules on amendments/corrections. The November 2016 edition is the authoritative version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity with the EPC and Implementing Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines give instructions on the practice and procedure to be followed in the various aspects of the examination of European applications and patents in accordance with the European Patent Convention and its Implementing Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All procedural and substantive examination practice described in the Guidelines is to be applied in conformity with the EPC and its Implementing Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination (Part A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part A outlines the procedures for formalities examination, mainly with regard to grant proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural steps and checks to be followed during formalities examination in grant-related processing are set out in Part A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search matters (Part B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part B deals with search matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions and standards for performing prior-art searches for European applications are contained in Part B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural aspects of substantive examination (Part C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part C contains the guidelines on procedures to be followed in substantive examination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers procedural conduct during substantive examination, including examiner and applicant interaction and decision-making steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition and limitation/revocation procedures (Part D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part D relates to procedures to be followed in opposition and limitation/revocation proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out the procedural framework, timings and requirements for filing, processing and deciding oppositions and related limitation/revocation matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: General procedural matters (Part E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part E summarises procedural matters relevant to several or all of the stages in proceedings before the EPO; it also contains information about the procedure before the EPO as designated or elected Office, applicable to Euro‑PCT applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Part E for cross-cutting procedural rules and for guidance when the EPO acts as a designated/elected Office (Euro‑PCT context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements of the European patent application (Part F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part F defines the requirements which the application must fulfil other than patentability, in particular unity of invention (Art. 82), sufficiency of disclosure (Art. 83), clarity (Art. 84) and the right to priority (Art. 87 to Art. 89).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F explains how to assess and apply non-patentability technical and formal requirements for European applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (Art. 82)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention is a requirement an application must fulfil (Art. 82).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on assessing whether claims belong to a single general inventive concept and how lack-of-unity issues are handled is provided in Part F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure (Art. 83)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art (Art. 83).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part F sets out how sufficiency is evaluated and what constitutes adequate disclosure in description and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (Art. 84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims and application content must meet the clarity requirements (Art. 84).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance addresses ambiguous claim language, claim support in the description, and how to remedy clarity issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to priority (Arts. 87–89)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part F covers the right to priority as provided for in Arts. 87 to 89.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains claiming priority from earlier applications, time limits, and formal requirements for priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Part G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part G deals with the requirements of patentability provided for in Art. 52 to Art. 57, in particular exclusions from patentability (Art. 52(2) and 53), novelty (Art. 54), inventive step (Art. 56) and industrial application (Art. 57).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G contains standards and assessment approaches for whether subject-matter is excluded from patentability, is novel, involves an inventive step, and is industrially applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from patentability (Art. 52(2) and Art. 53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain subject-matter is excluded from patentability under Art. 52(2) and Art. 53.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G explains categories of excluded subject-matter and application of exclusions in substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Art. 54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is a requirement under Art. 54 to be assessed against the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on the assessment of novelty, prior-art relevant date, and interpretation of disclosures is provided in Part G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (Art. 56)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventive step (non-obviousness) is required under Art. 56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part G sets out how to apply problem-solution approaches and other methods to determine whether claimed subject-matter involves an inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial application (Art. 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention must be susceptible of industrial application as required by Art. 57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance clarifies what constitutes industrial applicability and how to evaluate it for different technical fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and corrections (Part H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part H deals with the requirements relating to amendments and corrections, in particular to questions of admissibility (Rule 80 and Rule 137) and compliance with Art. 123(2) and (3), Rule 139 and Rule 140.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H explains when and how applications and patents may be amended or corrected, and the tests for admissibility under the cited EPC provisions and Implementing Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of amendments (Rule 80 and Rule 137)
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissibility of amendments during proceedings is governed by Rule 80 and Rule 137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance covers what changes are allowable during examination/opposition and procedural requirements for filing amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Art. 123(2) and (3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments must comply with Art. 123(2) (no added subject-matter) and Art. 123(3) (no extension of scope of protection after grant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part H provides the criteria and examples used to assess added matter and post-grant scope-extension concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction rules (Rule 139 and Rule 140)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules 139 and 140 set out correction mechanisms for errors in applications and patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains procedural routes and limits for correcting errors, and the standards for permitting such corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritative version and revisions (November 2016 edition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The November 2016 edition of the Guidelines is the only valid official version, and supersedes the November 2015 edition as from 1 November 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guidelines are frequently revised; users are advised to use the online version (HTML/PDF) which reflects the latest valid text. The HTML view offers a 'Show modifications' option to display inserted (green) and deleted (red strikethrough) text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and language formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guidelines are available online in the EPO's three official languages in both PDF and HTML format and also in printed format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to frequent revisions, prefer the online version which reflects the latest valid version in force.
